title: Week in Orbit
summary: The space and defense sectors are buzzing with activity this week, from acquisitions to new initiatives in lunar exploration. As the industry grapples with emerging technologies and geopolitical tensions, the focus remains on resilience and collaboration.

themes.title: Lunar Ambitions Heat Up
themes.body: The European Space Agency is on the hunt for lunar mapping capabilities to support its Argonaut lander, signaling a renewed interest in lunar exploration. This move may set the stage for increased international collaboration in the race to the Moon.

themes.title: Acquisition Frenzy Continues
themes.body: Rocket Lab's acquisition of Iridium is being touted as a logical next step, reflecting a broader trend of consolidation in the space sector. Expect more players to follow suit as they seek to bolster their capabilities and market positions.

themes.title: Quantum Concerns in Orbit
themes.body: As quantum computing advances, its implications for national security in space are becoming increasingly apparent. The industry must now grapple with how to safeguard sensitive information against potential quantum threats.

themes.title: Funding for Space Resilience
themes.body: The recent $1.4 billion boost to the space resilience line in the FY27 budget underscores the growing recognition of vulnerabilities in orbital operations. This funding will likely enhance capabilities to counter emerging threats and bolster national security.
